post_text:
Day 2/30 — ValueTask vs Task Allocation Traps (.NET & C#)

Spotted a hot path in a profiler session generating massive Gen0 garbage collection spikes because synchronous cache hits still allocated state machines on the heap.

• **Task Allocations:** Returning a standard Task always allocates an object reference on the heap, even when the data is already in memory.
• **ValueTask Struct:** Returning ValueTask avoids heap allocations on synchronous completion by wrapping a union of T and Task.
• **IValueTaskSource:** Async continuations pool the backing source to prevent Gen0 overhead.

Watch out: Never await a ValueTask multiple times or consume it concurrently.

Have you audited your caching layers for hidden Task allocations lately?
